This notebook demonstrates entity matching from zero-shot through trained modes.
Part 1 shows zero-shot matching with cosine similarity. Part 2 measures how training
data quantity affects accuracy.

## Part 1: Zero-Shot Matching

```{python}
#| label: setup
#| cache: true
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from novelentitymatcher import Matcher

entities = [
    {"id": "DE", "name": "Germany", "aliases": ["Deutschland", "Bundesrepublik"]},
    {"id": "FR", "name": "France", "aliases": ["Frankreich", "La France"]},
    {"id": "US", "name": "United States", "aliases": ["USA", "America"]},
    {"id": "JP", "name": "Japan", "aliases": ["Nihon", "Nippon"]},
    {"id": "CN", "name": "China", "aliases": ["Zhongguo"]},
    {"id": "BR", "name": "Brazil", "aliases": ["Brasil"]},
    {"id": "IN", "name": "India", "aliases": ["Bharat"]},
    {"id": "GB", "name": "United Kingdom", "aliases": ["UK", "Britain", "England"]},
    {"id": "AU", "name": "Australia", "aliases": ["Oz"]},
    {"id": "CA", "name": "Canada", "aliases": ["Canuck Land"]},
]

matcher = Matcher(entities=entities, mode="zero-shot")
matcher.fit()
```

```{python}
#| label: match-examples
#| cache: true
queries = [
    "Deutchland", "America", "Frankreich", "Nihon", "UK",
    "Brasil", "Bharat", "Canuck Land", "Zhongguo", "Oz",
]

results = []
for q in queries:
    r = matcher.match(q, top_k=3)
    batch = r if isinstance(r, list) else [r]
    for entry in batch:
        entry["query"] = q
    results.extend(batch)

df = pd.DataFrame(results)
df[["query", "id", "name", "score"]].head(15)
```

```{python}
#| label: similarity-chart
#| cache: true
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
for q in ["Deutchland", "America", "Frankreich"]:
    r = matcher.match(q, top_k=10)
    batch = r if isinstance(r, list) else [r]
    labels = [e.get("id", "?") for e in batch]
    scores = [e.get("score", 0) for e in batch]
    ax.plot(labels, scores, "o-", label=q, alpha=0.7)

ax.set_xlabel("Entity")
ax.set_ylabel("Cosine Similarity")
ax.set_title("Similarity Profiles for Three Queries")
ax.legend()
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Part 2: Training Impact

```{python}
#| label: training-sweep
#| cache: true
training_pairs = [
    ("Deutschland", "DE"), ("Allemagne", "DE"),
    ("Frankreich", "FR"), ("France", "FR"),
    ("United States of America", "US"), ("Vereinigte Staaten", "US"),
    ("Nihon", "JP"), ("Japan", "JP"),
    ("Zhongguo", "CN"), ("Chine", "CN"),
    ("Brasilien", "BR"), ("Brasil", "BR"),
    ("Bharat", "IN"), ("India", "IN"),
    ("Großbritannien", "GB"), ("United Kingdom", "GB"),
    ("Australien", "AU"), ("Australia", "AU"),
    ("Kanada", "CA"), ("Canada", "CA"),
]

test_queries = [
    ("Deutchland", "DE"), ("America", "US"), ("Frankreich", "FR"),
    ("Nihon", "JP"), ("UK", "GB"), ("Brasil", "BR"),
    ("Bharat", "IN"), ("Canuck Land", "CA"), ("Zhongguo", "CN"), ("Oz", "AU"),
]

sweep = {}
for n in range(0, len(training_pairs) + 1, 2):
    texts = [t for t, _ in training_pairs[:n]]
    labels = [l for _, l in training_pairs[:n]]
    mode = "zero-shot" if n == 0 else None
    m = Matcher(entities=entities, mode=mode)
    if n > 0:
        m.fit(texts=texts, labels=labels)
    else:
        m.fit()
    correct = sum(
        1 for q, expected in test_queries
        if (r := m.match(q)) and isinstance(r, dict) and r.get("id") == expected
    )
    sweep[n] = correct / len(test_queries)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))
xs = list(sweep.keys())
ys = list(sweep.values())
ax.plot(xs, ys, "o-", color="#3498db", linewidth=2, markersize=6)
ax.fill_between(xs, ys, alpha=0.1, color="#3498db")
ax.set_xlabel("Training Samples")
ax.set_ylabel("Accuracy")
ax.set_title("Accuracy vs Training Size")
ax.set_ylim(0, 1.05)
ax.axhline(y=sweep[0], color="#e74c3c", linestyle="--", alpha=0.5,
           label=f"Zero-shot baseline ({sweep[0]:.0%})")
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
ax.legend()
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(plt.FuncFormatter(lambda y, _: f"{y:.0%}"))
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

**Key insight:** Even 4–6 training samples per entity can significantly boost accuracy over zero-shot, thanks to SetFit's few-shot learning.
